nodes.label: Perceptual Salience
nodes.definition: Relative perceptual prominence of a stimulus feature or object that can bias selection priority.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Perceptual prominence contributes to competition for selection but does not guarantee capture.

nodes.label: Attentional Set / Target Template
nodes.definition: An active representation of goal-relevant target properties that biases selective attention.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Goal-relevant representations alter competition for attentional selection.
failure_modes: Assuming a marketing persona proves an attentional set
open_questions: Naturalistic inference from search intent and task context

nodes.label: Executive Attentional Control
nodes.definition: Control processes that regulate attentional competition in accordance with task goals.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Executive control can bias selection and resolve interference while interacting with working-memory representations.
failure_modes: Treating one reaction-time score as global executive control

nodes.label: Reward-Associated Attentional Priority
nodes.definition: Attentional priority acquired through prior associations between features and reward or learned value.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Learning history can persistently bias later selection, but magnitude is method-sensitive.
failure_modes: Using prior likes as direct evidence of value-driven capture
open_questions: Transport from visual-search paradigms to copy exposure

nodes.label: Prior-Selection History
nodes.definition: Bias in current attentional priority attributable to prior selections independently of current goals or physical salience.
exclusions: reward learning when reward association is the primary mechanism
nodes.mechanism_summary: Past selection episodes can alter future priority.

nodes.label: Sustained Attention
nodes.definition: Maintenance of task-relevant attentional engagement over an extended interval.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Sustained attention concerns ongoing task-relevant processing rather than initial selection.
failure_modes: Inferring sustained attention from early hold or completion rate alone

nodes.label: Vigilance Decrement
nodes.definition: Decline in performance or attentional maintenance as time-on-task increases under vigilance demands.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Performance may degrade over sustained monitoring time.
failure_modes: Calling any drop-off a vigilance decrement without task controls

nodes.label: Attentional Disengagement
nodes.definition: Process of releasing or shifting attentional priority away from the currently selected target.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Disengagement governs release from current priority and can shape switching/reorientation.

nodes.label: Certainty Appraisal
nodes.definition: Appraisal of how certain or predictable an event, cause, or outcome appears within an emotional episode.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Certainty appraisal contributes to differentiated emotional response patterns.
failure_modes: Confusing emotional certainty appraisal with epistemic confidence

nodes.label: Controllability / Coping-Potential Appraisal
nodes.definition: Appraisal of whether and how a person can control, cope with, or respond effectively to an event or its consequences.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Perceived control and coping potential contribute to emotion differentiation and action tendency.
failure_modes: Assuming objective control equals perceived control

nodes.label: Affective Arousal
nodes.definition: Degree of affective activation or energetic intensity, analytically separable from positive-negative valence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Arousal can alter readiness and, in some contexts, social transmission, but its meaning depends on appraisal and context.

nodes.label: Approach Action Tendency
nodes.definition: Readiness or tendency to move toward, engage with, acquire, confront, or otherwise act in an approach-oriented direction.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Appraisal and affect can organize approach-oriented action readiness, but valence does not map one-to-one onto approach.
open_questions: Distinct approach forms in commercial decisions

nodes.label: Withdrawal / Avoidance Action Tendency
nodes.definition: Readiness or tendency to withdraw from, avoid, escape, or disengage from a target or situation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Appraisal and affect can organize withdrawal/avoidance readiness, but negative valence does not map one-to-one onto avoidance.
open_questions: Threat versus disgust versus effort-based avoidance

nodes.label: Self-Relevance
nodes.definition: Degree to which information, outcomes, or identities connect to a personally important aspect of the self.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Self-relevance can alter valuation, attention and processing by linking information to self-representations.
failure_modes: Inferring self-relevance from demographic targeting alone

nodes.label: Self-Categorization
nodes.definition: Psychological classification of self as a member of a salient social category, affecting self-perception and social influence.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Salient self-categorization can make group norms and prototypes self-relevant.

nodes.label: In-Group Prototypicality
nodes.definition: Degree to which a person, source, or position is perceived as representative of a salient in-group.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Prototypicality can shape who is influential when a group identity is salient.
failure_modes: Using surface similarity as proof of prototypicality

nodes.label: Perceived Source Genuineness / Authenticity
nodes.definition: Perception that a source's self-presentation or communication is genuine rather than fabricated or strategically false in a way relevant to evaluation.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Genuineness can contribute to source evaluation, especially in relational or influencer contexts, with contextual heterogeneity.

nodes.label: Source Reliability Track Record
nodes.definition: Historical evidence or perception that a source has produced dependable outcomes or accurate/reliable information over time.
nodes.mechanism_summary: Past reliability can inform source evaluation but is domain-specific and evidence for an independent stable construct is not yet sufficient here.
failure_modes: Treating past reliability as guaranteed current accuracy
open_questions: Best construct placement versus evidence-traceability module
